title: Firebomb thrown at Grameen Bank office in Natore
excerpt: Attackers threw bottles with burning cloth onto a Grameen Bank office in Baghatipara, after an arson attack on its Sylhet zonal office on 15 November.
content:
Unidentified attackers threw bottles fitted with oil-soaked cloth onto the veranda of a Grameen Bank office at Bashbaria in Natore's Baghatipara upazila late on Monday night (16 November), bdnews24.com's Bangla edition reported. The night guard, Nasir Uddin, saw flames and alerted staff, who put the fire out. No one was hurt and there was no significant damage.

Police recovered two 250 ml glass bottles and a plastic bottle. Sumon Chandra Das, officer-in-charge of Baghatipara Police Station, said police could not yet confirm whether the device was a petrol bomb.

Two days earlier, at about 3:50am on 15 November, arsonists set fire to Grameen Bank's Sylhet zonal office, burning documents and an officer's car, the same outlet reported. Grameen Bank had already said that 22 of its branches in 16 districts were set on fire or targeted between 10 and 17 November, and the UN has called for an investigation.

Why it matters

The attacks keep spreading. Grameen Bank's branches hold the savings and loan records of its members, and an attack can cut them off from services. Other microfinance institutions and NGOs with field offices across the country face the same risk to staff and premises, and many will be reviewing their security plans.

What to watch

Whether police identify and charge those behind the attacks, whether the government steps up protection for microfinance and NGO offices, and whether services to members are disrupted.
